## 1. Open Studio on the Flows pillar

Three flows, all shipped with forge: one drafts a roadmap, one takes a decomposed initiative to a reviewed PR, one writes a project’s docs.

![Open Studio on the Flows pillar](/media/stories/S4/01-open-studio-on-the-flows-pillar.png)

## 2. Press "+ New flow"

The builder opens on a skeleton rather than an empty page: plan, then dev, then review.

![Press "+ New flow"](/media/stories/S4/02-press-new-flow.png)

## 3. Name the flow and say what it is for

A flow’s goal is not decoration: it is what every agent in it is told it is working towards, so it is written before the stations are.

![Name the flow and say what it is for](/media/stories/S4/03-name-the-flow-and-say-what-it-is-for.png)

## 4. Drag the "architect" agent out of the palette onto the canvas, and wire it into "plan"

This is the act the builder exists for.

![Drag the "architect" agent out of the palette onto the canvas, and wire it into "plan"](/media/stories/S4/04-drag-the-architect-agent-out-of-the-pale.png)

## 5. Open Advanced and bind gitpulse’s knowledge base to the flow

A flow that plans work on a project should read what forge already knows about it.

![Open Advanced and bind gitpulse’s knowledge base to the flow](/media/stories/S4/05-open-advanced-and-bind-gitpulse-s-knowle.png)

## 6. Seed the flow’s starter agents — the roster forge offers, only if the operator asks

The roster forge offers is not the roster you get.

![Seed the flow’s starter agents — the roster forge offers, only if the operator asks](/media/stories/S4/06-seed-the-flow-s-starter-agents-the-roste.png)

## 7. Press "Save Flow"

Saving is where forge judges the flow rather than the operator: the stations have to resolve to real agents, the edges have to carry artifacts the next station can read, and a name already taken is refused rather than overwritten.

![Press "Save Flow"](/media/stories/S4/07-press-save-flow.png)

## 8. Check the flow came out clean and can be started

A saved flow is not necessarily a runnable one.

![Check the flow came out clean and can be started](/media/stories/S4/08-check-the-flow-came-out-clean-and-can-be.png)

## 9. Open the launcher

How a flow is launched follows from what its first station is.

![Open the launcher](/media/stories/S4/09-open-the-launcher.png)

## 10. Point the flow at story-s4, describe the first piece of work, cap what the run may spend, and press "Start architect"

A flow built ten minutes ago is now dispatching a real Agent against a real repository, so the operator sets the ceiling before starting rather than discovering the bill afterwards.

![Point the flow at story-s4, describe the first piece of work, cap what the run may spend, and press "Start architect"](/media/stories/S4/10-point-the-flow-at-story-s4-describe-the-.png)

## 11. While it works, check Monitor

Monitor is the one surface that answers "what is running, and what is stuck".

![While it works, check Monitor](/media/stories/S4/11-while-it-works-check-monitor.png)

## 12. Open the session from Monitor, answer the Architect's questions about the work, and wait for it to finish drafting

The session is the same shared surface every kind of agent run uses, so a flow the operator built themselves is watched exactly the way the shipped ones are.

![Open the session from Monitor, answer the Architect's questions about the work, and wait for it to finish drafting](/media/stories/S4/12-open-the-session-from-monitor-answer-the.png)

## 13. Open the plan and stand at the verdict

This is where S4 ends: a flow the operator assembled, linted and launched has produced a plan, and forge is holding it at a gate for a decision.

![Open the plan and stand at the verdict](/media/stories/S4/13-open-the-plan-and-stand-at-the-verdict.png)
